# Access Tokens: Who am I?

Last updated on 2023-05-14

The contents of this article

Through the introduction of the above two parts, we understand that the Lark app is controlled by two dimensions,** permission scope **and **availability**, when it is designed and developed. With appropriate permission scopes, data communication can be achieved through Lark's OpenAPI or SDK API.

**The authentication method** is to tell Lark server "who is currently accessing this API" when the API is called. In other words, it allows Lark to know "who is accessing what tenant data now and in what capacity."

## Token categories

Access tokens available for the Lark API include the following three types:

- `tenant_access_token` **:** Tenant authorization token. With this token, the app uses its own account to perform corresponding actions, such as obtaining the information of a user from the contacts. The value of this token is prefixed with `t-`, for example: `t-24b5bf4e054bcef00b2af38a0b04f0af6d315b18`
- `app_access_token` **:** App authorization token. The open platform identifies the caller’s app, and the app can access information related to itself and not attributed to a specific company or user, such as obtaining the identity of the user currently logged into the app. The value of this token is prefixed with `a-` or `t-` , for example: `a-24b5bf4e054bcef00b2af38a0b04f0af6d315b18`

Note: In practical use, the `app_access_token` and `tenant_access_token` of the API response may be the same. This is due to the fact that `app_access_token` is used in fewer scenarios, and these two tokens are gradually unified on the Lark Open Platform.

- `user_access_token` **:** User authorization token. With this token, the app will perform actions on behalf of the user, such as creating a Docs or an Event through API. The value of this token is prefixed with `u-`, for example: `u-Lr1RT7S8fJUES03mT5FtWf`

You need to fill the access token into the request header parameter of the HTTP request when you call the API. Each Open API has an API that specifies the type of access tokens required and the way to obtain them.

![](https://sf16-sg.larksuitecdn.com/obj/open-platform-opendoc-sg/2bc1998649a0a6707923f2f39e0e91d7_nbdoSyEvDK.png)

*(Figure10: Description of the tokens in the server-side API)*

For more information about Lark access token, refer to [API access token overview](https://open.larksuite.com/document/ukTMukTMukTM/uMTNz4yM1MjLzUzM). Before the official start of development, developers are suggested to have a good understanding of Lark's access token mechanism.

> Note: The tokens should be placed in the HTTP request header and the value needs to be prefixed with``Bearer<space>`' , as shown below:

![](https://sf16-sg.larksuitecdn.com/obj/open-platform-opendoc-sg/f07a73f26a8fb0c28798765d4bdd9407_zW4y68CF97.png)

*(Figure11: Illustration of access token in the request)*

Use cURL sample code as follows:

```
curl --location --request GET`https://open.larksuite.com/open-apis/contact/v3/departments/od-64242a18099d3a31acd24d8fce8d9f9c' \--header`Authorization: Bearer t-5888bcb7c421a695ca83c449caba5c0b12becfda' \--header`Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8'
```

- **About expiration mechanism of tokens**

Access tokens have a validity period, so developers need to refresh the tokens on their own server side to prevent expiration. The maximum validity period of a generated token is 7200 seconds (2 hours); If the token is retrieved within the first 1.5 hours, the same value as the original value will be returned, but the remaining valid time (`expire`) will change each time it is returned, as shown below:

![](https://sf16-sg.larksuitecdn.com/obj/open-platform-opendoc-sg/27715420288e32dfbfd58c6fe864fbf6_lz9AWPZ4TR.png)*(Figure12: Expiration date of access token)*
